n-k-l1b-02.title: Which bus Hana go take today?
n-k-l1b-02.topic: Hangul for real life: bus-stop board
n-k-l1b-02.goal: Decide which information for bus board and text you need to identify correct bus, notice condition for brackets, and explain your choice.
n-k-l1b-02.material:
You and your friend Hana dey for bus stop wey dem call 시장 앞. Days: 월 Mon, 화 Tue, 수 Wed, 목 Thu, 금 Fri, 토 Sat, 일 Sun. 매일 mean every day.

[버스 정류장: 시장 앞]
3번 (월~금): 학교 · 병원
5번 (매일): 공원 · 병원 · 역
7번 (매일): 시장 · 학교

Hana text: ‘오늘은 일요일이에요. 병원에 가요. 몇 번 버스예요?’
n-k-l1b-02.thinking.1: Notice condition wey hide inside brackets
n-k-l1b-02.prereq.1: Know days of the week (월 ~ 일), numbers + 번
n-k-l1b-02.s.s1.prompt: To tell Hana bus number, which information you need? Choose all wey apply.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s1.hint.0: First write wetin Hana wan do, then ask which part for board answer am.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s1.hint.1: Read wetin dem write for brackets after each bus number. Wetin you need know about today to use am?
n-k-l1b-02.s.s1.o.b: Name of the stop where you dey
n-k-l1b-02.s.s1.r.b: You don already dey the stop. The board no change based on the name, so stop name no decide the bus.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s1.o.d: The board lines wey list that place
n-k-l1b-02.s.s1.o.e: How much the bus fare be
n-k-l1b-02.s.s1.r.e: Price no change which bus go reach the place, and board no show any price.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s1.explain: You need the place (병원), board lines wey list am, and today day, because 3번 dey run only 월~금. Stop name and fare no help choose the bus number.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s2.prompt: Which bus Hana suppose take today?
n-k-l1b-02.s.s2.hint.0: Cross out buses wey no list that place.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s2.hint.1: For buses wey remain, check bracket against today day.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s2.r.a: 3번 dey go 병원, but bracket say e dey run only 월~금, and today na 일요일.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s2.r.b: 7번 dey go 시장 and 학교. 병원 no dey the list.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s2.r.d: Both list 병원, but 3번 no dey run today, so dem no be the same.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s2.explain: 5번 list 병원 and e dey run 매일. 3번 list 병원 too, but e dey run only 월~금, and today na Sunday.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s3.prompt: Reply Hana for English (you fit add Korean words): which bus she suppose take, and why no take the other bus wey dey go there too?
n-k-l1b-02.s.s3.hint.0: Talk the bus number first, then give reason for one sentence.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s3.hint.1: Mention the day for today text and bracket on the other bus.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: I name one bus and talk why e fit today?
n-k-l1b-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: I talk why the other bus no fit today?
n-k-l1b-02.s.s3.model.0: Take bus 5. Bus 3 dey go hospital too, but e dey run only Monday to Friday, and today na Sunday.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s3.model.1: 5번 na the one. 3번 na only 월~금, so e no dey run Sunday.
n-k-l1b-02.s.s3.model.2: Hana suppose take 5. The 3 say Mon-Fri only, but today na 일요일.

n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.hint.0: Decide using only wetin you don read so far.
n-k-l1b-03.title: Two name tags, one family?
n-k-l1b-03.topic: Hangul for real life: read names and name tags
n-k-l1b-03.goal: Read Korean name tags, work out which part na family name, and change your guess about how two people relate as new information come.
n-k-l1b-03.material: First day for Korean class. You read name tags on desks and hear people introduce themselves. Korean names get family name first, then given name. For this class, every family name get one syllable (like 박, 김, 이). No space dey between names on tags.
n-k-l1b-03.thinking.0: Separate wetin name show from wetin e no show
n-k-l1b-03.thinking.1: Change your judgement when new information come
n-k-l1b-03.thinking.2: Tell wetin certain and wetin possible
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.prompt: Read each part and choose the statement wey you sure pass. Then continue.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.hint.1: Ask yourself: this one certain, or e only possible?
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.0.info:
Two name tags for desks:
박지민
박지훈
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: Wetin you fit talk for sure?
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.0.after: Both tags start with 박, so family name na the same. The tags alone no show whether dem relate.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: E possible, but no certain. 박 na common family name, so people wey get am often no be family.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Dem get the same family name.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Dem get the same given name.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: The given names different (지민 and 지훈).
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Two tags for two desks. The given names different too.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now wetin you know about 지민 and 지훈?
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.1.after: 지훈 talk am direct: 지민 na im younger sibling. So the same family name 박 fit mean family for this case, but na wetin he talk tell us.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.1.o.a: 지민 na younger brother or sister of 지훈.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: 지훈 talk say 지민 na 제 동생, ‘my younger sibling’, no be teacher.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.1.o.c: 지민 na older sister of 지훈.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: 동생 mean younger sibling. Older sister na 누나 or 언니.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.1.r.d: 지훈 talk 제 동생, so dem be family, no be only classmates.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.2.after: ‘동생’ and age no show the gender, and people use name 지민 for both. Nothing so far show whether 지민 na boy or girl.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Na girl, because 지민 sound like girl name.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: People use name 지민 for boys and girls, so name no be evidence.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Na boy, because 지훈 na boy and dem get same family name.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Everybody for the family share family name, and e no tell if person na boy or girl.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.2.o.c: We never know yet. Nothing wey dem talk so far show am.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Na boy, because older siblings na boys.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.st.2.r.d: 지훈 na the older one. Nothing talk say older one na boy, and dem no talk anything about younger one.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s1.reflect: Name show family name and given name, no be whether people relate or whether person na boy or girl. Every new information narrow wetin we know, and we separate ‘possible’ from ‘certain’.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s2.prompt: Now na your turn to introduce yourself as 박지민. Write two short lines for Korean (polite speech): greet, then talk your name.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s2.hint.0: Start with greeting wey you use for class.
n-k-l1b-03.s.s2.hint.1: Think how to say name politely: which ending follow am, and your name end with bottom consonant?
n-k-l1b-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: I greet and write my name for two lines?
n-k-l1b-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: I put family name first if I talk both parts?
n-k-l1b-03.s.s2.modelNote.3: This one natural too: you fit leave out subject 저는.

n-k-l1c-01.title: Who dey teach who for the photo?
n-k-l1c-01.topic: Subject, object and particles: who do wetin
n-k-l1c-01.goal: Decide which captions fit photo, test your clue with new caption, and explain why similar-looking caption mean opposite.
n-k-l1c-01.material: Class newsletter get photo: 수진 dey teach 민수 how to draw. Five students suggest caption. Words: 가르쳐요 = teach(es). Particles: 이/가 follow person wey do something; 은/는 follow topic (‘as for ...’); 을/를 follow person wey action happen to.
n-k-l1c-01.thinking.0: Use markers, no be position, to tell the roles
n-k-l1c-01.thinking.1: Use evidence to reject tempting reading
n-k-l1c-01.thinking.2: Explain rule to person wey think with English word order
n-k-l1c-01.prereq.1: Know 이/가 and 을/를 (the doer and receiver)
n-k-l1c-01.s.s1.prompt: For photo, 수진 dey teach 민수. Which captions describe this photo? Choose all wey apply.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s1.hint.0: No read names from left to right. First find which name get 이/가 or 은/는 and which get 을/를.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s1.hint.1: For each caption ask: whose name get 를 (or 을) after am, and dem teach that person or na that person dey teach?
n-k-l1c-01.s.s1.r.b: Particle 가 dey on 민수, so 민수 na the teacher here. This na opposite of photo.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s1.r.d: 수진 come first, but 을 dey on 수진: na her dem dey teach and 민수 dey teach. Word order no be clue.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s1.explain: For a, c and e, 수진 get 이/가 or 은/는 (the doer or topic), and 민수 get 를 (the person wey dem dey teach). The name order fit change; particles still show the roles.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.prompt: New caption appear: 동생을 엄마가 안아요. (안아요 = hug(s), 엄마 = mom, 동생 = younger sibling.) Who hug who?
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.hint.0: Find the particle after each name before you read their order.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.hint.1: Ask which particle show person wey do the action and which show person wey receive am.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.o.a: 엄마 hug 동생, because 엄마 get 가 and 동생 get 을.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.o.b: 동생 hug 엄마, because 동생 na the first name for sentence.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.r.b: First name no always be the person wey do something. 동생 get 을, so dem dey hug 동생.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.o.c: Dem hug each other, because both names get particle.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.r.c: The two particles different. 가 mark person wey hug and 을 mark person wey dem hug.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.o.d: We no fit tell, because the names dey in unusual order.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.r.d: You fit tell: particles keep the roles even when the order change.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s2.explain: 가 dey on 엄마 (person wey hug) and 을 dey on 동생 (person wey dem hug), so caption mean mom hug her younger sibling. Particles, no be order, show the roles.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s3.prompt: Friend read am with English word order and talk: ‘수진을 민수가 가르쳐요 start with 수진, so 수진 dey teach.’ For one or two English sentences, explain why this caption no fit the photo.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s3.hint.0: Point to particle next to 수진 and particle next to 민수.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s3.hint.1: Talk wetin each particle tell you about the role of its name.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: I name the particle wey dey on 수진?
n-k-l1c-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: I talk who dey teach for this caption?
n-k-l1c-01.s.s3.model.0: 수진 get particle 을, so na her dem dey teach; 민수 get 가, so 민수 dey teach. Position no decide am.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s3.model.1: Particles show the roles, no be order: 을 mark 수진 as receiver and 가 mark 민수 as doer, so e mean 민수 teach 수진.
n-k-l1c-01.s.s3.model.2: Because 가 show say na 민수 dey teach.

n-k-l1c-02.title: Where 민호 do wetin? Check diary
n-k-l1c-02.topic: Place particles: 에 (go, dey) and 에서 (do)
n-k-l1c-02.goal: Find lines for short diary wey use wrong place particle, talk rule wey separate 에 from 에서, and correct the lines.
n-k-l1c-02.material: Learner 민호 write him day for Korean. Some place particles wrong. Words: 아침 = morning, 점심 = lunch time, 오후 = afternoon, 저녁 = evening, 운동해요 = exercise(s).
n-k-l1c-02.thinking.0: Find mistake by checking every line against rule
n-k-l1c-02.thinking.1: Talk the rule behind the pattern
n-k-l1c-02.prereq.1: Know 에 and 에서 dey exist (place particles)
n-k-l1c-02.s.s1.prompt: This na 민호 diary about one day. Some lines get place particle mistake (more than one). Choose any line wey get am.
n-k-l1c-02.s.s1.hint.0: Underline verb and place particle for each line. Which lines look alike?
n-k-l1c-02.s.s1.hint.1: Group lines by their verb, then see which particle each group use.
n-k-l1c-02.s.s1.explain: Lines 3, 5 and 7 wrong: 도서관에서 책을 읽어요 (action for place), 집에 있어요 (being for place), 공원에서 운동해요 (action for place). Lines 1, 2, 4 and 6 okay.
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.prompt: Which rule explain difference between 에 and 에서 for this diary?
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.hint.0: Group correct lines by their verbs: which verbs go with 에 and which with 에서?
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.hint.1: Ask: verb mean person dey move or stay, or person dey do something there?
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.o.a: 에 show place where action happen; 에서 show place person go to or stay at.
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.r.a: That one reverse. Check 학교에 가요 (go to) and 식당에서 먹어요 (eat at).
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.o.b: 에 for big places like school; 에서 for small places like room.
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.r.b: Size no matter: 학교에서 and 집에서 both work for action.
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.o.c: 에 and 에서 mean same thing; you fit use either with any verb.
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.r.c: Dem different: 도서관에 책을 읽어요 sound wrong to Koreans.
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.o.d: 에서 show place where action happen; 에 show place person go to or stay at.
n-k-l1c-02.s.s2.explain: 에서 = place where you do something (eat, read, study, exercise). 에 = place you go to, or where person or thing dey (가요, 와요, 있어요).
n-k-l1c-02.s.s3.prompt: Now rewrite EVERY line wey get mistake, correctly. Write corrected sentences for Korean and keep verbs.
n-k-l1c-02.s.s3.hint.0: For every wrong line decide: person dey go there, stay there, or do something there?
n-k-l1c-02.s.s3.hint.1: Read your sentence loud: person dey do something for that place, or dey go there or dey there?
n-k-l1c-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: I use 에서 for actions and 에 for being at a place?
n-k-l1c-02.s.s3.modelNote.2: This one okay too: the place na destination, then action follow.

n-k-l1c-03.title: Can 지나 and 톰 meet for the library?
n-k-l1c-03.topic: Time and place: who dey where and when
n-k-l1c-03.goal: Choose facts wey matter for meeting (place AND time for both people), decide with dem, then suggest correction for Korean.
n-k-l1c-03.material:
Two messages for tomorrow. 오전 = morning (a.m.), 오후 = afternoon (p.m.), 저녁 = evening, 시장 = market, 집 = home.

지나: 저는 내일 오전에 도서관에서 한국어를 공부해요. 오후에는 시장에 가요.
톰: 저는 내일 오전에 집에 있어요. 오후에는 도서관에 가요. 저녁에 친구를 만나요.
n-k-l1c-03.prereq.1: Know basic 에 (going, being) and 에서 (doing)
n-k-l1c-03.s.s1.prompt: 지나 wan study with 톰 for library tomorrow, morning or afternoon. Which facts you need to know if this fit work? Choose all wey apply.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s1.hint.0: Read the question again: which people and which time of day e mention?
n-k-l1c-03.s.s1.hint.1: For every option ask: if I know this, e go change my decision about meeting?
n-k-l1c-03.s.s1.r.b: Question na only morning or afternoon; evening no be part of am.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s1.r.f: Question na only morning or afternoon; evening no be part of am.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s1.explain: To compare, you need each person place for each time wey question ask: 지나 morning and afternoon, 톰 morning and afternoon. Evening no matter for this plan.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.prompt: Now decide: 지나 and 톰 fit study together for library tomorrow, as the messages stand?
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.hint.0: Fill small table: person, morning place, afternoon place.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.hint.1: Check every option against your table, one by one.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.o.a: No. 톰 no go library tomorrow.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.r.a: 톰 talk 오후에는 도서관에 가요, so he dey go library.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.o.b: No. Dem dey at library at different time of day.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.o.c: Yes. Both of dem dey go library tomorrow.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.r.c: Both mention library, but at different times of day. Check 오전 and 오후.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.o.d: Yes. Both of dem dey at library in the morning.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.r.d: 톰 dey home (집에 있어요) in the morning.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s2.explain: 지나 dey at library in morning (도서관에서 공부해요) and go market in afternoon. 톰 dey home in morning and go library in afternoon. Both dey at library tomorrow, but never same time.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s3.prompt: Write short message for Korean from 지나 to 톰 (polite -요) to suggest time (오전 or 오후) to study together for library.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s3.hint.0: Choose time of day when one of you fit change plan.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s3.hint.1: Name the time, place, then end with request to study together.
n-k-l1c-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: The time I choose really work for both of us (one person must change a plan)?
n-k-l1c-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: I use 에 for time and for going to library?

n-k-l1c-04.title: Make sentence card: who, where, wetin
n-k-l1c-04.goal: Use roles of doer, place and thing (with their particles) to build correct sentence of your own, and check other cards with same rules.
n-k-l1c-04.material: Game with sentence cards. Words: 동생 = younger sibling, 공원 = park, 빵 = bread, 카페 = cafe, 식당 = restaurant, 시장 = market, 사요 = buy(s), 읽어요 = read(s).
n-k-l1c-04.thinking.2: Find role swap wey look okay at first glance
n-k-l1c-04.s.s1.prompt: Sentence-card game get four rules: (1) doer + 이/가 or 은/는, (2) place + 에서, (3) thing + 을/를, (4) verb last. Which sentences follow all four? Choose all wey apply.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s1.hint.0: Check one rule at a time. Underline particle on each part.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s1.hint.1: Remember which part each particle mark: doer, place, thing.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s1.r.a: The thing (빵) no get 을/를. People often leave am out when speaking Korean, but card rules need am.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s1.r.b: Particles swap places: this one say bread dey eat sibling.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s1.r.d: 공원에 mark place wey you go to; for place where you eat, card need 에서.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s1.explain: c and e get all four parts: doer 동생이, place 공원에서, thing 빵을, verb 먹어요 at the end. Middle parts fit change order; verb remain last.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s2.prompt: Make your own card. Write one Korean sentence about someone (you, friend, family) wey dey eat or drink something at a place. Follow all four rules, and end verb with -아요/어요.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s2.hint.0: Decide three parts first: who, where, wetin.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s2.hint.1: Add particles one by one, then put verb last and add -아요/어요.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: I fit point out the doer, place and thing for my sentence?
n-k-l1c-04.s.s3.prompt: Your classmate make four cards. One card get wrong particles, so roles mix up. Choose am.
n-k-l1c-04.s.s3.hint.0: Read each card by asking: who dey do am, and wetin dem dey do am to?
n-k-l1c-04.s.s3.hint.1: The doer na person wey fit really do the action?
n-k-l1c-04.s.s3.explain: Line 3 say book dey read sibling: 이 dey on 책 and 를 dey on 동생. Correct writing: 동생이 책을 읽어요.

n-k-l1c-05.title: Who dey eat cake? Chat keep changing
n-k-l1c-05.topic: Who do the action: read verb and particles
n-k-l1c-05.goal: Change your idea of who dey do action as chat add one sentence at a time, separate wetin dem state from wetin dem only suggest, and write negative sentence with correct roles.
n-k-l1c-05.material: Family chat about cake: Mom (엄마), Dad (아빠), younger sibling (동생) and speaker (저). The sentences come in three parts.
n-k-l1c-05.thinking.2: Read the verb before you decide who dey do wetin
n-k-l1c-05.s.s1.prompt: Read family chat one part at a time. Words: 만들어요 = make(s), 좋아해요 = like(s), 먹어요 = eat(s), 안 + verb = no do. Choose reading wey fit wetin you don read so far.

n-k-l1c-05.s.s1.st.1.o.a: 동생 probably go chop am, since 동생 like am.
n-k-l1c-05.s.s1.st.1.o.b: 동생 make am, because 동생이 dey first.

n-k-l1c-05.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Na only 엄마 go chop am, because she make am.
n-k-l1c-05.s.s1.st.1.r.c: New sentence na about 동생, no be 엄마.

n-k-l1c-05.s.s1.st.2.o.d: 저 dey chop am and 아빠 no; 동생 only likely.
n-k-l1c-05.s.s1.reflect: Every new sentence change the answer. At first, nobody know who dey chop; then likely eater show; then one person no fit be am. Check which verb you dey read before you decide who do am.
n-k-l1c-05.s.s2.prompt: Look back all three parts. Which statement text prove (no be just suggest)?
n-k-l1c-05.s.s2.hint.0: For every statement, find sentence about that person and read the verb.
n-k-l1c-05.s.s2.hint.1: For each statement ask: text talk am, or e only make am likely?

n-k-l1c-05.s.s2.r.b: 동생 like am, and that suggest so, but liking no be eating.

n-k-l1d-02.title: Friend shopping list for convenience store
n-k-l1d-02.goal: Turn short Korean text and price table into different shopping baskets wey meet every condition, then report one basket for Korean.
n-k-l1d-02.material:
Your friend text before you go convenience store:

‘편의점에 가요? 부탁해요!
칠천오백 원 있어요.
물 두 개 사요.
김밥하고 빵도 사요.
모두 일곱 개 사요.’

[가격표]
물 한 개: 오백 원
빵 한 개: 천 원
김밥 한 개: 이천 원
김밥 두 개: 사천 원
김밥 세 개: 사천오백 원
김밥 네 개: 육천 원

(Text say your friend get 7,500 won, buy 2 water bottles, want 김밥 and bread too, and buy 7 things in total.)
n-k-l1d-02.thinking.1: Read price table wey no simply price multiply by quantity
n-k-l1d-02.prereq.1: Know Sino-Korean numbers up to thousands (천, 오백, 칠천) and 원
n-k-l1d-02.prereq.2: Know native counts with 개 (한 개 ... 일곱 개)
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.prompt: Check 김밥 rows for price list. Which statement true?
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.hint.0: Read each 김밥 row as ‘number of gimbap: total price for all dem’.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.hint.1: Compare price for each quantity of gimbap with price of one gimbap.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.o.a: Each piece of gimbap cheaper when you buy more: 3 cost 4,500 won.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.o.b: Each 김밥 cost 2,000 won, so 3 김밥 cost 6,000 won.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.r.b: List say 세 개: 사천오백 원, so 3 김밥 cost 4,500 won, no be 6,000.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.o.c: 김밥 cost more: 4 gimbap cost 8,000 won.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.r.c: List say 네 개: 육천 원, so 4 김밥 cost 6,000 won.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.o.d: Two gimbap cost 3,000 won, one cheaper than 1 + 1.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.r.d: List say 두 개: 사천 원, so 2 gimbap cost 4,000 won.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s1.explain: Table list total price for each set: 1 gimbap 2,000; 2 gimbap 4,000; 3 gimbap 4,500; 4 gimbap 6,000. Price no always be 2,000 times quantity.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s2.prompt: Find 2 different baskets wey fit EVERYTHING for text. g = number of gimbap, b = number of bread (the 2 bottles water already fixed).
n-k-l1d-02.s.s2.hint.0: First write conditions with your own words: how much money, how many things in all, and wetin must dey inside.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s2.hint.1: Count the 2 water bottles too. Then test possible gimbap quantities one by one.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s2.hint.2: For every try, add water, gimbap (from LIST), and bread, then compare with 7,500 won.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s2.ok.c1: Both gimbap and bread dey included.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s2.fail.c1: 김밥하고 빵도 사요: buy at least one of each.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s2.ok.c2: Seven things total, including the 2 water bottles.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s2.fail.c2: 모두 일곱 개: with the 2 water bottles, gimbap and bread must add up to 5.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s2.fail.c3: More than 7,500 won (칠천오백 원). Remember water total cost 1,000 won, and use price LIST for gimbap.

Use price list, no be 2,000 times quantity, make 3 gimbap fit.
n-k-l1d-02.s.s2.because.prompt: Choose ONE basket and text your friend for Korean (polite -요): how many gimbap, how many bread, and total price including water.

n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.prompt: Which rule fit ALL six sentences?
n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.hint.0: Make two columns: wrong sentences and correct ones. Wetin stay same inside each column?
n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.hint.1: Test each rule with one sentence wey e suppose explain. E fit explain others too?
n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.o.a: Both number types always correct; speaker fit choose freely.
n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.r.a: Three sentences sound wrong, so choice no free.
n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.o.b: Wetin you dey count decide which number system fit.
n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.o.c: Small numbers use native (하나, 둘 ...) and big numbers use Sino (이십오, 이만 ...).
n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.r.c: 오월 오 일 use small number 5 as Sino, and 이십오 살 big but need native 스물다섯, so number size no decide.
n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.o.d: Native numbers for casual speech, Sino numbers for polite speech.
n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.r.d: Same numbers appear in polite speech: 세 개 주세요 and 이만 원이에요 both polite.
n-k-l1d-05.s.s2.explain: Counting word na the key. Things, people, ages and hours (개, 명, 살, 시) use native numbers; money, minutes, months, dates and numbers like bus 3 (원, 분, 월, 일, 번) use Sino numbers.
n-k-l1d-05.s.s3.prompt: Show Tom pattern with your OWN two Korean sentences (write numbers in Hangul): one with native number plus 개, 명, 살 or 시; another with Sino number plus 원, 분, 월, 일 or 번.
n-k-l1d-05.s.s3.hint.0: First sentence: choose something you fit count (apples, students, your age).
n-k-l1d-05.s.s3.hint.1: Second sentence: choose price, number of minutes or date.
n-k-l1d-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: My first sentence count things, people, age or hours with native number?
n-k-l1d-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: My second sentence give money, minutes, date or number with Sino number?
n-k-l1d-05.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Tom fit see pattern from my two sentences?
n-k-l1d-05.s.s3.modelNote.1: Age with native number; minutes with Sino number.

n-k-l1a-01.title: Junho reads shop labels aloud.
n-k-l1a-01.topic: Read Hangul: vowels wey look alike.
n-k-l1a-01.goal: Find readings in classmate list wey mix up similar vowels, name mistake type, and correct readings.
n-k-l1a-01.material: Junho dey learn Hangul. He read 6 shop labels aloud and write readings beside each word. Letter sounds: ㅏ=a, ㅓ=eo, ㅗ=o, ㅜ=u, ㅣ=i, ㅡ=eu; ㄱ=g, ㄴ=n, ㄷ=d, ㅁ=m, ㅂ=b, ㄹ=r/l; block wey start with ㅇ start with vowel sound. Some readings wrong.
n-k-l1a-01.prereq.0: Knows Hangul letters and basic sounds.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose one line where Junho reading no match Hangul. (More than one wrong.)
n-k-l1a-01.s.s1.hint.0: Read each block using letter sounds, then compare with Junho reading.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s1.hint.1: Compare vowel in each block with vowel in his reading, one block at a time.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s1.explain: Lines 2 and 4 wrong. 구두 has ㅜ (u), so na gu-du, no be go-du. 거미 has ㅓ (eo), so na geo-mi, no be ga-mi. Other 4 lines match.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s2.hint.0: For each wrong line, list letters wey change between Hangul and Junho reading.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s2.hint.1: Change na consonant, vowel, or block order?
n-k-l1a-01.s.s2.o.a: He mix two similar consonants, like ㄱ and ㅋ.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s2.r.a: Consonants ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅁ in wrong lines read correct as g,d,m. Change na vowel.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s2.o.b: He mix vowels wey look alike: stroke dey other side/end (ㅜ/ㅗ, ㅓ/ㅏ).
n-k-l1a-01.s.s2.o.c: He read blocks in wrong order, last one first.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s2.r.c: Both readings keep block order (go-du same order as gu-du). Only vowel sound change.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s2.o.d: He forget say ㅇ at start of block no get sound.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s2.r.d: Words starting with ㅇ (우유) read correct, and wrong lines no start with ㅇ.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s2.explain: In both wrong lines vowel change: ㅜ become o, ㅓ become a. These vowels differ only by where short stroke sit. Similar-looking vowels common first mistake.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s3.prompt: Write correct Latin reading of 2 wrong words (like na-mu), then add short tip to help Junho tell similar vowels apart.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s3.hint.0: Compare your own reading of both wrong words, block by block.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s3.hint.1: Tip gats say where short stroke sit: above, below, left or right of long line.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Each reading use only letter sounds given?
n-k-l1a-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: My tip show where each vowel stroke dey?
n-k-l1a-01.s.s3.model.0: gu-du and geo-mi. Tip: ㅜ stroke dey below line, ㅗ stroke dey above.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s3.model.1: 구두=gudu, 거미=geomi. Tip: ㅓ short stroke point left; ㅏ stroke dey right.
n-k-l1a-01.s.s3.model.2: gu-du / geo-mi. Remember: 'up' vowel ㅗ na o; 'down' vowel ㅜ na u.

n-k-l1a-02.title: The small bottom letter na just decoration?
n-k-l1a-02.topic: Read Hangul: final consonant (받침) change word.
n-k-l1a-02.goal: Judge classmate claim about final consonant (받침) with evidence from price tag and payment, then explain in your own words.
n-k-l1a-02.material: At market, Jiwoo and Hajun check apple bag price tag. Needed numbers: 이=2, 삼=3, 사=4, 오=5, 천=1,000 (이천 원=2,000 won). Jiwoo reads tag as 삼천 원. Hajun says: 'Small letter at bottom just decoration, so 삼 and 사 same, I read 사천 원.'
n-k-l1a-02.thinking.1: Notice small detail fit change meaning.
n-k-l1a-02.prereq.0: Can read Hangul blocks with final consonant.
n-k-l1a-02.prereq.1: Knows numbers 이, 삼, 사, 오 and 천.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.prompt: Test Hajun rule on number list: what does it say about 삼 and 사 blocks, and does list agree?
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.hint.0: Cover bottom letter of 삼 with finger. Which block remain?
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.hint.1: Compare that block with number list. Would rule still give 2 different numbers?
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.o.a: Dem go be same word and list agree: 삼=3 and 사=3.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.r.a: List no talk so. E give 삼=3 and 사=4, two different numbers.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.o.b: They look different by hand, but in print same block.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.r.b: In print too, 삼 and 사 different blocks: one has ㅁ bottom and other none.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.o.c: Under that rule they become same word, but list gives 삼=3 and 사=4, so rule fail.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.o.d: Rule no concern them because neither block has bottom letter.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.r.d: 삼 has ㅁ below vowel. Na exactly bottom letter wey rule talk about.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s1.explain: Hangul block read as whole, including final consonant. If bottom letter decoration, 삼 and 사 same word, but list say 삼(sam)=3 and 사(sa)=4. So rule fail; check Jiwoo 삼천 원 against payment.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s2.prompt: New evidence: Jiwoo pays with 5,000 won note and clerk returns 2,000 won. Which tag does this support?
n-k-l1a-02.s.s2.hint.0: Calculate how much Jiwoo spend: money paid minus change.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s2.hint.1: Check which of 4 tags give that amount.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s2.r.b: Then 5,000−2,000=3,000 would be change, no be 2,000.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s2.explain: 5,000−2,000=3,000. Payment match Jiwoo reading 삼천 원, no be Hajun 사천 원, so bottom letter matter.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s3.prompt: In 1 or 2 sentences, explain to Hajun why bottom letter no be decoration. Use 삼천 원 as example.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s3.hint.0: Compare 삼 and 사 letter by letter.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s3.hint.1: Say wetin extra letter add to block and number each block mean.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: I say wetin bottom letter do to block?
n-k-l1a-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: I show with block pair, like 삼 and 사?
n-k-l1a-02.s.s3.model.0: Bottom letter ㅁ part of block. Without am, block na 사 (4); with am, na 삼 (3). So price tag say 3,000 won, no be 4,000.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s3.model.1: 삼 and 사 na different words: 삼=3 and 사=4. Bottom letter change number, so e no be decoration.
n-k-l1a-02.s.s3.model.2: Bottom letter change word: 가 and 간 different. Same way 삼(3) and 사(4) differ, so bottom letter matter.

n-k-l1a-03.title: The torn sign above door.
n-k-l1a-03.topic: Read Hangul: syllable blocks on signs.
n-k-l1a-03.goal: Decide what information you need to read half-covered sign, say wetin certain, and read final word when dem show more.
n-k-l1a-03.material: Sign above department store door torn. You fit read only first 2 blocks: 화장. Two words for this floor start like this: 화장실 (restroom), 화장품 (makeup). You want restroom.
n-k-l1a-03.thinking.0: See wetin both possible words share.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s1.prompt: Which information help you tell which word sign say?
n-k-l1a-03.s.s1.hint.0: Write 2 possible words one under other and underline same part.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s1.hint.1: Ask which part of sign fit differ between both words.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s1.r.a: Both words start same 2 blocks 화장, so reread no fit tell them apart.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s1.o.b: See next block after 화장 on sign.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s1.r.c: Color no be part of written word; any color door fit carry either word.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s1.r.d: Floor tell where you dey, no be which word torn sign show.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s1.explain: Both words differ only for third block (실 or 품). First 2 same, so third block alone fit decide.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s2.prompt: Friend call ask: 'Wetin sign say?' Reply in 1 or 2 short Korean or English sentences: say wetin you fit read sure and wetin you never know.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s2.hint.0: Say which blocks you fit read.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s2.hint.1: Add wetin you still need see before you name word.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: I separate part wey I fit read from the one I no fit?
n-k-l1a-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: I avoid choosing a word without evidence?
n-k-l1a-03.s.s2.model.0: I fit read 화장, but I never know the third block. E fit be 화장실 or 화장품.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s2.model.1: The first two blocks talk say 화장. I no fit say the whole word until I see the third block.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s2.model.3: I fit read 화장 but I never read the third block; I need see am to know the word.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s3.prompt: The paper move and the third block show. E get ㅍ (top), ㅜ (vowel), and ㅁ (bottom). Which door e be?
n-k-l1a-03.s.s3.hint.0: Join the top letter, vowel, and bottom letter into one block.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s3.hint.1: Compare that block with the two possible blocks 실 and 품.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s3.r.a: The restroom word get block 실; the letters dem show give different block, 품.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s3.o.b: Either one; the first two blocks enough.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s3.r.b: The third block decide between the two words, and now you fit see am.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s3.o.d: Neither; you no fit read the sign.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s3.r.d: Now you fit read all three blocks, so you fit read the sign.
n-k-l1a-03.s.s3.explain: Letters ㅍ + ㅜ + ㅁ make block 품, so the sign say 화장품 (makeup). Restroom no dey behind this door.

n-k-l1a-04.title: A paper on restaurant wall
n-k-l1a-04.topic: Reading Hangul: signs with one or two words, similar-looking blocks
n-k-l1a-04.goal: Read paper wey dem cover in three steps, no decide too early, and notice how two words wey look alike (있어요, 없어요) change the meaning.
n-k-l1a-04.material: Somebody tape paper on restaurant wall. Hand cover most of am and move small-small each time. Words wey fit help: 있어요 = there is, 없어요 = there is not.
n-k-l1a-04.thinking.0: Waiting till you get enough evidence
n-k-l1a-04.thinking.2: Separating two blocks wey look alike
n-k-l1a-04.prereq.0: Can read Hangul blocks with final consonants
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.prompt: Read each part, choose answer wey fit wetin you fit read so far, then continue.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.hint.0: Use only the letters wey you fit see so far.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.hint.1: Ask yourself what other word fit start with the same block or same word.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.0.info: You fit see only one block: 김
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.0.after: 김 start 김치, 김밥, and the common family name 김 too. One block no enough to decide, so waiting make sense.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.0.o.c: I no fit know yet; more than one word start with 김.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.0.o.d: Name tag: 김 na common family name.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Family name na another guess. One block no show whether na a name, 김치, or 김밥.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.1.info: The hand move. Now you fit read the first word: 김치
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.1.after: You know the topic (kimchi), but you no know wetin dem say about am. Next word go tell you.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.1.o.a: The paper dey talk about kimchi, but I no know wetin e say about am.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Nothing yet say 'sale'. Paper wey name food fit be menu, price, warning, or notice.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: There is no word about free or price yet.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.1.r.d: There is no word about taste yet.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.2.info: The hand move away. The whole paper: 김치 없어요.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.2.after: 없어요 (there is not) get bottom letters ㅂ + ㅅ; 있어요 (there is) get only ㅆ. The paper say kimchi no dey.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: The last word get two letters under vowel (ㅂ and ㅅ), so na 없어요, no be 있어요. The two words look alike but mean opposite things.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Nothing on the paper talk about price.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.st.2.r.d: The paper no ask anybody to bring anything; e just state say something no dey.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s1.reflect: First block rarely tell the whole sign, and food name alone no show wetin the paper say about am. The last word decide the meaning, and e differ from the similar word only by the bottom letters.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s2.prompt: Write wetin the paper say with your own words (English or Korean). Then name the word wey decide the meaning.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s2.hint.0: First, say the whole message in English.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s2.hint.1: Then point to the one word wey fit change the whole message if e change.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: I talk the meaning, no be only the Hangul?
n-k-l1a-04.s.s2.selfAssess.1: I name the word wey change the meaning?
n-k-l1a-04.s.s2.model.0: E say kimchi no dey. The last word 없어요 decide am; 있어요 go mean the opposite.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s2.model.1: 김치 없어요 = no kimchi. The second word, 없어요, na the important one.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s2.model.2: Dem don finish the kimchi. The last word (없어요) tell me, no be the first word.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s3.prompt: Another paper get the same cover. You fit read 물, then one covered word wey fit be 있어요 or 없어요. Wetin you must see before you fit tell wetin the paper say?
n-k-l1a-04.s.s3.hint.0: Write the two possible messages under each other and underline the difference.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s3.hint.1: Ask yourself which part of the paper fit still change one message into the other.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s3.o.a: Bottom letters of covered word: one letter (ㅆ) or two (ㅂ + ㅅ).
n-k-l1a-04.s.s3.o.b: The first block 물 again, but read am more slowly.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s3.r.b: You fit already read 물. Reading am again no show which of the two final words dem cover.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s3.r.c: Colour no be part of the written message.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s3.o.d: Nothing else; 물 by itself only tell me say water dey.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s3.r.d: Drink or food name only give the topic. 있어요 and 없어요 mean opposite things.
n-k-l1a-04.s.s3.explain: 물 only give the topic. The two last words look alike and differ in bottom letters, so you must see those letters to know whether paper say water dey or no dey.

n-k-l1a-05.title: Make a look-alike quiz for your class
n-k-l1a-05.topic: Reading Hangul: similar-looking consonants and word pairs
n-k-l1a-05.goal: Choose a good look-alike pair, make your own pair of real Korean words, and explain how to tell them apart.
n-k-l1a-05.material: Your teacher ask every student to make one look-alike quiz: two real Korean words wey look almost the same because only one letter different. Example idea: 가 and 나 (one letter different).
n-k-l1a-05.thinking.0: Setting a condition for a good example
n-k-l1a-05.thinking.1: Making an example wey meet the condition
n-k-l1a-05.thinking.2: Explaining a difference with your own words
n-k-l1a-05.prereq.1: Can recognize shapes ㅁ/ㅂ, ㅏ/ㅓ, ㄴ/ㄷ
n-k-l1a-05.s.s1.prompt: Which pair make a good look-alike quiz item?
n-k-l1a-05.s.s1.hint.0: Write wetin stay the same and wetin change between the two words for each choice.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s1.hint.1: Good item get a difference wey you fit point at with your finger.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s1.r.a: Every block different; this no be look-alike pair.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s1.r.c: One word dey inside the other and the length different; this no be one-letter difference.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s1.r.d: The two words written exactly the same, so nobody fit tell them apart by reading.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s1.explain: 물 and 불 na both real words, and only first letter different (ㅁ vs ㅂ). Good quiz need two real words, one small difference, and difference you fit point to.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s2.prompt: Make your own pair: write two real Korean words wey differ by one letter (no use pair printed in this task), then add their English meanings.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s2.hint.0: Think of one word you know well, then change one letter.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s2.hint.1: Check say the new block too make a real word.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Both words real Korean words wey I know?
n-k-l1a-05.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Dem differ by exactly one letter?
n-k-l1a-05.s.s2.model.2: 눈 (eye) and 문 (door): the first letter different.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s3.prompt: Write one or two sentences to tell classmate how to tell your two words apart (which part differ and where).
n-k-l1a-05.s.s3.hint.0: Say which block, and which letter inside am, different.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s3.hint.1: Say whether difference dey top, middle, or bottom of block.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: My classmate fit find am from my sentence?
n-k-l1a-05.s.s3.model.0: The first letter different: ㄷ for 달 and ㅁ for 말. The rest of the block same.
n-k-l1a-05.s.s3.model.1: Check the bottom letter: 공 get ㅇ below and 곰 get ㅁ. First letter and vowel ㅗ same.

n-k-l1b-01.title: The sign painter wey write wetin e hear
n-k-l1b-01.topic: Hangul for everyday life: spelling versus sound of final consonants
n-k-l1b-01.goal: Find shop signs wey copy sound instead of spelling, understand why sound alone no fit give spelling, then write the signs correct.
n-k-l1b-01.material: Dongho paint signs for market street. Friend read shop names aloud, and Dongho write each one the way e sound. Below dey six signs with English meaning. These na everyday words you don study in class.
n-k-l1b-01.thinking.0: Separating wetin you hear from wetin dem write
n-k-l1b-01.thinking.1: Finding mistakes by checking each line against wetin you know
n-k-l1b-01.thinking.2: Explaining why one sound fit come from different written letters
n-k-l1b-01.prereq.0: Can read Hangul with final consonants (받침)
n-k-l1b-01.prereq.1: Knows 꽃, 옷, 신발, 과일, 빵 as vocabulary
n-k-l1b-01.s.s1.prompt: Some of Dongho signs get spelling mistake. Choose one line wey spelling wrong.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s1.hint.0: Choose one sign word you know from class and spell am from memory. The bottom letter match the sign?
n-k-l1b-01.s.s1.hint.1: Say each sign aloud, then compare last letter of each word with the spelling you know.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s1.explain: Lines 2 and 4 spelling wrong. Flower shop na 꽃 가게 and clothes shop na 옷 가게. Line 6 correct: dem write 밥 with ㅂ at bottom, the way the word spell.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.prompt: Dongho write signs by copying wetin e hear. Why copying sound fit lead to wrong spelling?
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.hint.0: Say 꽃 and 옷 aloud. Their last sounds tell you which bottom letter dem write?
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.hint.1: Ask: if two different letters sound the same, you fit know from sound which one dem write?
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.o.a: Na only ㄷ dem fit write at bottom of block, so Dongho signs correct.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.r.a: Many letters fit dey at the bottom (ㅂ for 밥, ㅁ for 삼, ㅅ for 옷). ㄷ na only one of dem.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.o.b: People no pronounce bottom letters at all, so Dongho no fit hear dem.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.r.b: People pronounce bottom letters; sound just no always be the written letter (옷 dey sound like [옫]).
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.o.c: Shop signs get special spelling wey different from normal words.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.r.c: Signs use normal spelling. People write 꽃 as 꽃 everywhere, on signs and in books.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.o.d: Different bottom letters fit make same sound, so sound alone no show spelling.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s2.explain: At the bottom of a syllable, ㅅ, ㅈ, ㅊ, ㅌ (and others) all sound like ㄷ. So [꼳] fit come from 꽃, and one sound fit have more than one spelling. You must know written word, no be only sound.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s3.prompt: Write the signs wey spelling wrong again with correct Hangul.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s3.hint.0: Take the two lines you find and change only the word wey get bottom-letter mistake.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s3.hint.1: Use spelling from textbook, no be the sound in your head.
n-k-l1b-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Both signs show the written word, not only the sound?
n-k-l1b-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: I keep the shop word (가게 or 집) after each one?
n-k-l1b-01.s.s3.modelNote.1: Joined spelling or 집 dey work too.

n-k-l1b-05.prereq.0: Can read Hangul with final consonants (받침)
n-k-l1b-05.title: Rule wey get exception: you pronounce bottom letter?
n-k-l1b-05.topic: Hangul for real life: final consonants and the sounds you pronounce
n-k-l1b-05.goal: Test friend rule about final consonants with real words, make your own counter-example, and choose rule wey fit all words.
n-k-l1b-05.material: Tom, your classmate, get this rule: ‘The letter at the bottom of a syllable na the sound you pronounce at the end. 밥 pronounce [밥]. 집 pronounce [집].’ Tom test am with list of words. [ ] show how dem pronounce each word.
n-k-l1b-05.thinking.2: Change the rule so e fit the facts
n-k-l1b-05.prereq.1: Know the words 밥, 집, 책, 물, 옷, 꽃, 밖, 맛, 낮
n-k-l1b-05.s.s1.prompt: Which words break Tom rule? Choose all wey apply.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s1.hint.0: For each word, compare bottom letter of the written word with bottom letter of the sound for [ ].
n-k-l1b-05.s.s1.hint.1: Word break the rule when the two no match.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s1.r.a: Bottom letter ㅂ pronounce as ㅂ, so rule hold. E no be counter-example.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s1.r.c: Bottom letter ㅂ pronounce as ㅂ, so rule hold.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s1.r.e: Bottom letter ㄹ pronounce as ㄹ, so rule hold.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s1.explain: 옷 [옫], 꽃 [꼳] and 밖 [박] pronounce with different bottom sound from the written letter (ㅅ, ㅊ and ㄲ). 밥, 집 and 물 follow Tom rule, so one counter-example enough to show say the rule no always true.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s2.prompt: Give ONE more counter-example of your own, a word wey no dey the list above. Write the word, how dem pronounce am for [ ], and one English sentence to explain wetin happen to bottom letter. Word bank if you need am: 맛 (taste), 낮 (daytime), 밭 (field).
n-k-l1b-05.s.s2.hint.0: Choose word from the bank (or one wey you know) and talk am slowly: which sound you hear for the very end?
n-k-l1b-05.s.s2.hint.1: Write the word and sound for [ ], then check: bottom letter inside [ ] same as the written one?
n-k-l1b-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: My word na one where bottom letter no pronounce as written?
n-k-l1b-05.s.s2.selfAssess.1: I write the sound for [ ] and talk wetin the bottom sound be?
n-k-l1b-05.s.s2.model.0: 맛 [맏] - bottom letter ㅅ pronounce like ㄷ, no be like ㅅ.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s2.model.1: 낮 [낟]. The ㅈ for bottom sound like d, so dem no pronounce am as written.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s2.model.2: 앞 [압] → bottom letter ㅍ change to ㅂ.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.prompt: Now correct Tom rule. Which new rule fit ALL the words, including your own counter-example?
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.hint.0: Check each new rule with 밥 [밥], 옷 [옫], 꽃 [꼳] and 밖 [박].
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.hint.1: Reject rule if even one word for the list break am.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.o.a: Every bottom letter loud and clear pass, so ㅅ remain ㅅ and ㅊ remain ㅊ.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.r.a: Na Tom rule again. E fail for 옷 [옫] and 꽃 [꼳].
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.o.b: Every bottom letter disappear, so dem pronounce 옷 [오] and 꽃 [꼬].
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.r.b: Dem still pronounce bottom letter (as short stop). Dem no pronounce 밥 as [바].
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.o.c: Only few sounds fit end syllable: ㅅ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ → ㄷ, ㄲ ㅋ → ㄱ, ㅍ → ㅂ.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.o.d: Na only words for list special; every other word follow first rule.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.r.d: Words for list na examples only. Plenty more dey, so this no fit all of dem.
n-k-l1b-05.s.s3.explain: Na only few sounds dey used for bottom of syllable. Letters like ㅅ, ㅈ, ㅊ, ㅌ dey pronounce like ㄷ, and ㄲ and ㅋ like ㄱ, ㅍ like ㅂ. Dem still pronounce bottom letter, but no always the way dem write am.

n-k-l1b-04.title: Mina dey count the prices
n-k-l1b-04.topic: Hangul for real life: menu board and notes under am
n-k-l1b-04.goal: Check friend claim against the whole menu board, find the line of her reasoning wey fail, and explain am using note under menu.
n-k-l1b-04.material:
Mina and you dey snack shop. Mina look menu board and text you. The board:

[분식집 메뉴]
김밥 3,000원
라면 4,000원
떡볶이 4,000원
※ 점심 세트 (11시~2시) 김밥 + 라면 5,000원
(세트 = set meal)

Mina text: ‘지금 12시 30분이에요. 저는 6,000원 있어요. 김밥하고 라면은 7,000원이에요. 못 먹어요.’
n-k-l1b-04.thinking.0: Check claim against all the evidence for one page
n-k-l1b-04.thinking.1: Find the first step wey fail
n-k-l1b-04.prereq.0: Fit read Hangul and numbers in 천 원
n-k-l1b-04.prereq.1: Know 시 and 분 for time
n-k-l1b-04.s.s1.prompt: Mina talk say she no get money reach 김밥 + 라면. Check the whole board and time for her text. Wetin be the best judgement?
n-k-l1b-04.s.s1.hint.0: Check every line for the board, no be only prices, before you add anything.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s1.hint.1: Compare time for Mina text with times for board.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s1.r.a: This one use only single prices and skip note for bottom of board.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s1.o.b: Mina wrong: for 12:30, lunch set give both for 5,000, wey less than 6,000.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s1.o.c: Mina correct: set na only 김밥 and 떡볶이, so 라면 cost extra.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s1.r.c: The set line read 김밥 + 라면. E include 라면.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s1.o.d: Mina correct: lunch set finish before 12:30, so price na 7,000.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s1.r.d: Set dey run 11시~2시, and 12시 30분 dey inside those hours.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s1.explain: 11시~2시 na time for lunch set and 12시 30분 dey inside am. 김밥 + 라면 cost 5,000원 then, so Mina fit order both with 6,000원.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s2.prompt: Na Mina reasoning be this, line by line. Choose the FIRST line wey no true for 12:30.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s2.hint.0: Check the lines one by one from top and stop for the first one wey no match the board for 12:30.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s2.hint.1: For every line ask: the whole board, at that time, agree with am?
n-k-l1b-04.s.s2.explain: Line 3 na the first one wey fail: for 12:30, set make 김밥 + 라면 5,000원, no be 7,000원. Lines 1, 2 and 4 true. Line 5 false too, but na because line 3 false.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s3.prompt: Write short reply to Mina for English (Korean words dey okay) to show her the board evidence.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s3.hint.0: Start by telling Mina wetin she fit or no fit do, then give reason.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s3.hint.1: Talk which line for the board you use and wetin e talk about her situation.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s3.selfAssess.0: My reply point to the board line wey Mina miss?
n-k-l1b-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: I give the new price and compare am with 6,000?
n-k-l1b-04.s.s3.model.0: You fit order both. Na lunch time now (12:30), and 점심 set na 김밥 + 라면 for 5,000 won. You get 6,000.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s3.model.1: Check the ※ line: from 11 to 2, set cost 5,000원, less than your 6,000원, so you fit get both.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s3.model.2: 점심 세트 na 5,000원 until 2시. Now na 12:30, so 김밥 + 라면 na only 5,000 and your money reach.
n-k-l1b-04.s.s3.model.3: You correct say separately e cost 7,000, but for lunch time the set na 5,000 won, so you fit chop both.
